summary: This stylesheet defines the complete layout and styling for a report management page with a dashboard section and a list of report cards. It uses CSS Flexbox for layout, applies a design system with CSS variables for colors, and includes both light and dark mode support with hardcoded colors for specific report type badges.

explanations.3: This centers the page content horizontally by setting left and right margins to auto, which works because max-width creates a constraint.
explanations.8: Flexbox is being used to arrange child elements in a row; this will be used for the header layout.
explanations.9: Align-items: baseline means items line up based on their text baseline, useful for mixing different sized text elements like a title and back link.
explanations.21: This uses a CSS custom property (variable) defined elsewhere in the design system; the double-dash prefix indicates it's a variable, not a regular property.
explanations.36: The gap property creates space between flex items, similar to margin but cleaner for flexible layouts.
explanations.41: Flex: 1 means this input will grow to fill available space in its flex container.
explanations.43: This creates a border using a color variable; solid means a regular unbroken line.
explanations.51: Outline: none removes the browser's default focus ring, which they're replacing with a custom border color on line 52.
explanations.70: Flex-wrap: wrap lets summary cards drop to the next line if there isn't enough horizontal space.
explanations.75: Like the input field, flex: 1 makes cards grow to fill space, but min-width: 100px ensures they don't get too small.
explanations.78: Background-surface-color is a softer background shade than the page background, creating visual separation for card components.
explanations.129: Margin-left: auto pushes this link to the right side of the container by using all available left space.
explanations.140: This creates a thick colored line on the left of report text as a visual accent; think of it like a highlighter bar.
explanations.152: White-space: pre-wrap preserves line breaks and spaces in the text, useful for displaying code snippets or formatted context.
explanations.153: Overflow-wrap: break-word forces long words to break onto the next line instead of overflowing the container.
explanations.164: Inline-flex makes the badge display inline (like text) but with flexbox layout control, so it stays in the text flow.
explanations.224: Transition: opacity 0.15s smoothly animates opacity changes over 150 milliseconds, creating a subtle hover effect.
explanations.250: Background: none removes the default background, leaving only the border visible; this creates an outlined button style.
explanations.274: The attribute selector [data-theme="dark"] targets styles that only apply when dark mode is enabled.
